claims.text: Linktree reported that over one month Devin authored about 300 PRs and Linktree merged about 100 of them, mostly customer-reported bug fixes, small features, and prototypes of larger features.
Cognition reports that 67% of Devin's PRs are now merged, versus 34% the previous year.
Cognition reports Devin is 4x faster at problem solving and 2x more efficient in resource consumption than a year earlier.
The Citation Group merged 271 Devin PRs in the first three months, at an 80% success rate, after senior engineer review.
Cognition merged 659 Devin PRs into its own codebase in one week (reported 2026-02-27), up from 154 in its best week in 2025.

At Citation, unstructured prompts often produced inconsistent results, while tasks scoped in Jira with clear requirements and documentation pulled into Devin sessions generated PRs that passed review.

Citation identified three critical practices: Jira ticket scoping with clear acceptance criteria, Devin search-to-session to pull documentation and architectural context into a session, and Markdown specification files for structured inputs.

Linktree found Devin's success depends on the scope of the change and the amount of ambiguity Devin must overcome, and recommends using Devin for tasks an engineer could complete in a couple of hours.
Linktree reports Devin struggles with many tasks but has a very good success rate at instrumenting analytics event tracking, which they operationalized with a continually refined prompt.
Linktree used the knowledge feature to teach Devin which files to update in repos with many files, and ran five parallel Devins (one per repo/PR) to add new social platforms.
Cognition shared a Playbook script using the Devin API to automatically spawn multiple Devins to implement a whole multi-repo feature, which Linktree adopted.
Linktree advises concise, specific instructions without chit chat, and starting a new session on a sub-task when context gets too long.
Linktree had Devin attempt a PHP cron job feature despite expecting it to struggle; the attempt served as a proof of concept that led to a design discussion and the team completing the change.

A Cognition Playbook is like a custom system prompt for a repeated task, and should include the desired outcome, steps, postcondition specifications, advice correcting Devin's priors, forbidden actions, and required inputs from the person starting it.
Cognition uses Playbooks for complex recurring work such as ingesting data into Redshift, running database migrations, and integrating with Stripe, Plaid, and Modal.

Cognition's !triage-bug playbook fires when the Bug label is added to a Linear ticket, reads the report, searches code paths, checks git history, and posts root cause and suggested fix, using the Datadog MCP for logs.
Cognition gave Devin Datadog access and read-only database access so it can investigate bugs end to end and open a PR with a fix and regression test.
Devin Review's Autofix automatically fixes PRs when bugs are flagged and works on CI/lint issues until all checks pass; Cognition uses Devin Review on every PR because review became the bottleneck.
Session Insights analyzes completed Devin sessions for issues like scope creep and communication gaps, and suggests improved prompts for new sessions.
Cognition advises breaking large tasks into smaller isolated sessions, notes Devin has no phone for mobile testing, and says tasks needing extensive validation need verification mechanisms in place.
Devin does best with clear requirements, cannot independently handle ambiguous projects end to end, and needs human review when outcomes are not straightforwardly verifiable.
Devin handles upfront scoping well but performs worse when requirements change or are added mid-task, which puts more responsibility on engineers to scope work up front.

With Claude Sonnet 4.5, Cognition observed 'context anxiety': the model took shortcuts or left tasks incomplete when it believed it neared its context limit, even with room left; Cognition countered with reminders at both the start and end of prompts and by enabling the 1M token beta while capping usage at 200k.

Cognition found that relying on Sonnet 4.5's self-written notes without its own compaction and summarization systems caused performance degradation and knowledge gaps, because the notes sometimes paraphrased the task and omitted details.

In Devin's testing mode, early versions went off track by over-testing unrelated parts, getting lost in setup, or missing the PR's core behavior; Cognition now has Devin write a code-grounded test plan first and annotate expected behavior before each action, and remaining failure modes include screenshot timing misses and over-reliance on executing JavaScript instead of clicking through the UI.
